content.text: No non-solicitation, no-hire, or inducement covenant exists anywhere in the agreement. The only restrictive covenants on Client are compliance, access-limitation, and confidentiality obligations; the sole "solicit" hits concern unsolicited commercial e-mail (§ 7), which is unrelated. Since our playbook's **preferred** position is precisely the absence of any non-solicit binding the Customer, this is compliant with no redline needed.

input.rationale: The Agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-inducement covenant binding the Client. Targeted searches for "solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "recruit" and "personnel" returned no restrictive hiring covenant: the "solicit" hits are confined to § 7 (Unsolicited Commercial E-Mail), and the "employ"/"employees" hits are only the § 8(c) access-limitation covenant and the § 12 indemnity beneficiary lists. Full reads of the two likely host sections — § 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client) and § 10 (Confidentiality) — confirm Client's only covenants are compliance with laws, non-representation as to underwriting decisions, limiting Interface access, the Credit Data license, content warranties, and confidentiality. This matches our preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer"), so no redline is warranted; there is no duration, scope, or general-advertising carve-out to negotiate. Two notes for the file, neither a deviation: (1) § 8(d) references a separate "Non-Competition Agreement" governing use of Credit Data — that instrument is outside this document and should be reviewed separately for any personnel restrictions on Client; and (2) because the rule's preferred outcome is the absence of a clause, this is classified compliant rather than "missing".
